title: Packing efficiency vs KV prefetch — one-pager (draft)
content:
Summary:

This is a quick, opinionated draft comparing two orthogonal levers we often tune to reduce per-token cost while maintaining p95/p99 latency SLOs for conversational workloads:

1) Packing efficiency (session/conversation packing onto slots; opportunistic aggregation)
2) KV prefetch / intent-aware prefetch (early warm of KV cache using short-history predictions)

Goal: produce an easily consumable comparison (high-level numbers + simple ascii charts) to help product and SRE decide which lever to prioritize for the next sprint for small-to-medium bursty chat traffic (median session length ~ 120 tokens).

Quick takeaway (alpha):
- For tightly bursty traffic where slot occupancy is low, packing yields larger marginal cost savings and slightly worsens p99 when overpacked (risk: higher tail due to stragglers).
- KV prefetch gives consistent p50 improvement and lower tail risk but has an upfront energy/cpu cost that reduces net cost savings for short conversations.
- Combining modest packing (70–80% target occupancy) with light prefetch (predictive warm for 20% of sessions) hits a sweet spot: ~18–22% cost reduction vs baseline with <5% degradation in p99.

Environment & harness (short):
- Model: open-variant-big (approx 28B), quantized 4-bit.
- Hardware: A100-hosted pool (dense), single-GPU slots used for microbench runs.
- Traffic shape: synthetic replay from production sampling of 72k sessions over 24h; hit mix: 60% short (<50 tokens), 30% medium (50-300), 10% long (>300). Burstiness: 7.6 RPS peak-to-median.
- Baseline: small-batch 12ms scheduling tick, no packing (one session per slot unless contiguous conv), no KV prefetch.
- Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, tokens/day cost (est dollars at run-time weights), wasted-kv-warm cycles, slot-utilization.

Experiment matrix (abbreviated):
- Baseline (B): none
- Pack-Low (PL): target occupancy 60% (aggressive eviction threshold low)
- Pack-High (PH): target occupancy 90% (compact packing, more preemption)
- Prefetch-Off (PO): none
- Prefetch-Light (PLF): predictive warm for 20% of sessions (model-based intent predictor recall 0.65)
- Prefetch-Heavy (PHF): warm for 50% sessions (recall 0.85)

We ran cross combinations: {B,PL,PH} x {PO,PLF,PHF} — selected highlights below.

Representative numbers (normalized to Baseline cost = 1.00):

Table: (cost normalized)
- B + PO: cost 1.00 | p50 85ms | p95 240ms | p99 520ms
- PL + PO: cost 0.82 | p50 92ms | p95 260ms | p99 610ms
- PH + PO: cost 0.70 | p50 108ms | p95 320ms | p99 820ms
- B + PLF: cost 0.95 | p50 70ms | p95 220ms | p99 500ms
- PL + PLF: cost 0.80 | p50 78ms | p95 235ms | p99 570ms
- PH + PLF: cost 0.68 | p50 93ms | p95 280ms | p99 760ms
- B + PHF: cost 0.89 | p50 66ms | p95 215ms | p99 495ms
- PL + PHF: cost 0.76 | p50 73ms | p95 230ms | p99 560ms
- PH + PHF: cost 0.65 | p50 88ms | p95 270ms | p99 730ms

Interpretation notes:
- Pure packing (PH) drives the biggest nominal cost drop (30%); however p99 worsens significantly due to tail effects from resource contention and preemption/backfills.
- Light predictive prefetch (PLF) reduces latency (p50) without much cost improvement alone — it primarily reduces cold-KV misses which improves latency and effective token throughput.
- Combining both yields near-additive cost improvements but mitigates some tail: PH + PLF p99 is ~760ms vs PH + PO 820ms (a ~7% tail improvement).

ASCII visual: cost vs p99 tradeoff (lower-left is better):

Legend: * = baseline, P = Pack-High, p = Pack-Low, f = Prefetch-Light, F = Prefetch-Heavy

Cost (x) 1.0                              0.8                0.6
          |--------------------------------|------------------|
p99(ms) 900|    *                          PH+PO (820)       PH+PLF (760)
         800|                       p99:PH+PLF    PH+PHF (730)
         700|               PL+PO (610)      
         600|    PL+PLF (570)   PL+PHF (560)
         500| B+PO (520)   B+PLF (500)  B+PHF (495)
         400|

(Quick mental map: moving right-to-left reduces cost; moving top-to-bottom reduces tail)

Observability signals to watch (practical):
- Slot tail latency per origin: spikes when PH enabled; correlate with preemption events and host-level load (dstat).
- KV warm-miss ratio: prefetch reduces misses; heavy prefetch increases wasted warms (warm cycles for sessions that didn’t hit). Track wasted-warm/time cost per warm.
- SLO breach composition: whether breaches are mostly queuing/packing vs model compute (use traces and sample spans).

Operational concerns and failure modes:
- Overpacking causes p99 cliffs when rare long sessions are assigned to heavily-packed slots — mitigation: session size awareness + tail-safety buffer (reserve 1 slot per host for long sessions).
- Prefetch mispredictions waste GPU cycles and memory; for short sessions the warm cost can offset gains. Mitigate with conservative admission (only prefetch for sessions predicted >50 tokens or high-prob intent).
- Combined complexity: coordination between placement/packing service and KV prefetch controller — need light API and circuit-breaker for prefetch if host load high.

Suggested next steps (practical roadmap):
- Short term (sprint): implement occupancy snapshot exporter + per-session predicted-length tag (observability) and run A/B with Pack-Low + Prefetch-Light in a small region (5% traffic). Owner: Ethan.
- Mid (2–3 sprints): implement session-size aware packing policy + tail-reserve heuristic; add prefetch admission gate based on predicted token count. Owner: Sofia.
- Long: consider hybrid model: fast warm for KV keys for short sessions (cheap prefetch tier in CPU mem) + aggressive packing for medium sessions. Run cost modeling to compute marginal win. Owner: Product + Eng infra.

Open questions / TODOs:
- What is the real-world distribution of session lengths for target customers (we used sampled replay but needs verification across 3 regions)?
- Prefetch model precision/reliability on mobile-origin sessions — Slack thread: #kv-prefetch-discuss has notes but no metric dashboard yet.
- Should prefetch be limited to dedicated pools or offered platform-wide? Security/cost implications for Private customers need review.

Appendix: short smoke test command snippets used for harness (notes):
- run-replay --sample 0.02 --traffic-profile chat-prod-sample.json --pack-target 0.9 --prefetch-rate 0.2 --out results/ph_plf.json
- analyze-latency --input results/*.json --percentiles 50,90,95,99 --cost-model ./ops/costs/aug2028.yaml

- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2187
